title.narrative: Fiscal Management Efficiency Project (formerly Fiscal Management Reform Program II)

description.narrative: The project aims to ensure greater sustainability of public investments in Sri Lanka, particularly in the less developed regions, through more effective public resource management. It seeks to do so by enhancing the fiscal space (i.e., availability of greater resources) as a result of bringing about improved tax administration and compliance as well as more efficient public financial management. This will be largely attained through establishment of two management information system- one related to revenue and the other to expenditure management.

title.narrative: Loan 2624: 100% of contracts awarded and 100% disbursed as of 17 Jun 2022

Progress Toward Outcome: RAMIS is now fully operational and is aligned with the Inland Revenue Act, and is operating satisfactorily.
Despite delays, ITMIS was mostly developed using ADB funds and the ITMIS roll-out phase will be financed using government funds. ITMIS had still not been fully implemented at end-2018, the indicators associated with public expenditure management cannot ,therefore, be reasonably attributed to output 2.

Status of Implementation Progress: Output 1: Revenue Administration Management Information System (RAMIS) is now fully operational and is aligned with the Inland Revenue Act of 2017, and the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) is satisfied with its performance. RAMIS has enabled the automation of these core functions: registration, returns, tax payments, appeals, collections, cancellations, directions, clearances, and electronic filing, among others. The number of tax filers more than doubled during 2009 to 2018, from 150,000 to 318,941. Electronic filing of tax returns was introduced in March 2016, and laws and regulations are being prepared to require corporations to file electronically by December 2020. Each taxpayer is now provided a unique identification number. Computerized risk-based selection of audit files is not yet fully functional, but implementation is underway.
Output 2: Full Integrated Treasury Management Information System (ITMIS) development and roll out was set at 31 October 2018. On that date, however, only the budget planning module had been rolled out to all 190 spending agencies. In 2019, four more modules (budget appropriation, general ledger, system administration, and court cases) were rolled out to all agencies. Yet, the 2020 budget/vote on account was still prepared using the old system (CIGAS - Computerized Integrated Government Accounting System), due to the reorganization of ministries and changes in project headings. As of July 2020, four more core modules (receipt management, treasury management, revenue management, and expenditure management) have been rolled out to 16 departments within MOF, and they will be rolled out to the other 174 spending agencies through December 2021, along with the asset management and internal audit modules. By project closure in October 2018, the contractor had delivered and configured the hard infrastructure for ITMIS application.
Output 3: Through 2011, the Project Management Unit (PMU) identified training requirements and modalities and engaged training institutes. Ultimately, 660 staff were trained in 32 international programs and 855 more were trained in national programs on topics such as macroeconomics, e-governance and change management, strengthening public policymaking. Another 800 government users were trained in ITMIS and 1,500 in RAMIS. Basic computerized training was provided to about 1,200 officials at IRD and 650 officials at Treasury Operations Department of MOF.
